issues.title: Implement user registration
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can create an account so that my planning data is private.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Registration accepts email, display name, and password.
- [ ] Email addresses must be unique.
- [ ] Passwords are securely hashed and never stored as plain text.
- [ ] Invalid fields produce clear validation messages.
- [ ] Successful registration signs the user in or redirects them to sign in.
- [ ] Registration behavior is covered by automated tests.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add or update the registration form.
- [ ] Add registration route and validation.
- [ ] Hash passwords using an appropriate Flask-compatible library.
- [ ] Handle duplicate accounts.
- [ ] Add registration tests.

issues.title: Implement sign-in and sign-out
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can sign in and sign out so that I can securely access my workspace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid credentials create an authenticated session.
- [ ] Invalid credentials show a useful error without revealing sensitive details.
- [ ] Users can sign out.
- [ ] Dashboard and app routes reject anonymous users.
- [ ] Sessions use secure configuration appropriate to the environment.
- [ ] Authentication flows are covered by tests.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add sign-in and sign-out routes.
- [ ] Add authentication session management.
- [ ] Protect private routes.
- [ ] Add authentication tests.

issues.title: Enforce user data isolation
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can only access my own assignments and integration settings so that my data remains private.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every user-owned query is scoped to the signed-in user.
- [ ] A user cannot view, update, or delete another user's records.
- [ ] Unauthorized access returns an appropriate error.
- [ ] User isolation is tested for both page routes and JSON endpoints.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Audit all user-owned database queries.
- [ ] Add authorization helpers or service-layer checks.
- [ ] Add cross-user access tests.

issues.title: Create database-backed assignments
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can add an assignment so that PlanGuard can rank it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A signed-in user can create an assignment.
- [ ] Supported fields include title, course, deadline, difficulty, estimated minutes, course impact, progress, completion status, notes, and optional provider ID.
- [ ] Required fields and numeric ranges are validated.
- [ ] The assignment is stored in the database and belongs to the signed-in user.
- [ ] The new assignment appears on the dashboard.
- [ ] Creation success and failure cases are tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Finalize the Assignment model.
- [ ] Build the assignment form.
- [ ] Add create route and service logic.
- [ ] Replace hardcoded dashboard data.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Edit existing assignments
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can edit an assignment so that my plan stays accurate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can open an edit form populated with the assignment's current values.
- [ ] Updates validate required fields and sensible ranges.
- [ ] Only the owning user can edit the assignment.
- [ ] Saved changes immediately affect the dashboard and priority ranking.
- [ ] Update behavior is covered by tests.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add edit UI.
- [ ] Add update route and service logic.
- [ ] Recalculate priorities after updates.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Delete assignments
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can delete an assignment so that removed work no longer appears in my plan.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can request deletion from the dashboard or assignment detail view.
- [ ] The UI asks for confirmation before deletion.
- [ ] Only the owning user can delete the assignment.
- [ ] Deleted assignments no longer appear in the queue.
- [ ] Delete behavior is covered by tests.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add delete control and confirmation.
- [ ] Add delete route and authorization.
- [ ] Decide how related focus sessions are handled.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Track assignment completion and progress
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can mark an assignment complete or update its progress so that PlanGuard reflects my current workload.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Progress accepts values from 0 through 100.
- [ ] A user can mark an assignment complete or incomplete.
- [ ] Completed assignments are removed from or visually separated from the active queue.
- [ ] Changes trigger priority recalculation.
- [ ] Completion and progress behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add progress and completion controls.
- [ ] Persist changes.
- [ ] Update active/completed dashboard sections.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Build database-backed priority queue
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can see my assignments ranked by priority so that I know what to work on next.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Active assignments are loaded from the signed-in user's database records.
- [ ] The existing deterministic priority engine ranks each active assignment.
- [ ] The highest-priority assignment is clearly highlighted.
- [ ] Overdue assignments are handled clearly.
- [ ] Missing or edge-case data does not crash ranking.
- [ ] Ranking behavior is covered by tests.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Connect dashboard queries to the priority service.
- [ ] Sort active assignments by score.
- [ ] Add top-recommendation UI.
- [ ] Add overdue and edge-case handling.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Support available study time
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can set my available study time so that recommendations fit my day.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The user can enter or select available study minutes.
- [ ] Priorities recalculate when availability changes.
- [ ] Time-fit behavior is reflected in the recommendation.
- [ ] Invalid values are rejected with clear feedback.
- [ ] The preference persists for the expected session or account scope.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add availability input.
- [ ] Pass availability into the priority engine.
- [ ] Decide and implement persistence.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Explain each priority score
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can understand why an assignment received its score so that I trust the recommendation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each assignment displays its final priority score.
- [ ] The explanation includes deadline urgency, difficulty, course impact, time fit, and current progress.
- [ ] A plain-language explanation states why the assignment ranks high or low.
- [ ] The explanation is accessible from each assignment row.
- [ ] Explanation output is deterministic and tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Extend the priority service to return factor details.
- [ ] Create explanation copy rules.
- [ ] Add explanation UI.
- [ ] Add unit and route tests.

issues.title: Implement focus session timer
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can start a focus block from a recommendation so that I can begin studying quickly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A focus block can be started from the top recommendation.
- [ ] The timer displays elapsed or remaining time.
- [ ] The user can pause, resume, and end the session.
- [ ] Refresh or navigation behavior is handled intentionally.
- [ ] Timer controls are keyboard accessible.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Design focus-session states.
- [ ] Build timer UI and client-side behavior.
- [ ] Connect timer actions to persistence endpoints.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Persist focus sessions and history
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can save completed focus sessions so that I can review my study history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Focus sessions belong to a user and optionally an assignment.
- [ ] Start, pause, resume, and completion state changes are persisted as needed.
- [ ] Completed duration is stored.
- [ ] Recent focus history is visible.
- [ ] A user cannot access another user's sessions.
- [ ] Lifecycle behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add FocusSession model and migration.
- [ ] Add focus-session service and endpoints.
- [ ] Add recent-history UI.
- [ ] Add authorization and lifecycle tests.

issues.title: Update assignment progress after focus sessions
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can update assignment progress after a focus session so that future priorities adapt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ending a linked focus session offers a progress update.
- [ ] Progress remains between 0 and 100.
- [ ] Saving progress triggers priority recalculation.
- [ ] The user may finish a session without changing progress.
- [ ] The workflow is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add post-session progress UI.
- [ ] Update assignment service logic.
- [ ] Refresh recommendation data.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Recommend calendar-aware focus blocks
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can receive focus-block suggestions that avoid existing commitments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PlanGuard represents available study windows.
- [ ] Calendar events are treated as conflicts.
- [ ] Suggested blocks fit the assignment's estimated effort when possible.
- [ ] Large assignments may be split into multiple blocks.
- [ ] Users can accept, adjust, or dismiss suggestions.
- [ ] Scheduling behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Define scheduling data structures.
- [ ] Implement conflict detection.
- [ ] Implement block recommendation logic.
- [ ] Build suggestion controls.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Connect Google Calendar with OAuth
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can connect Google Calendar so that PlanGuard avoids scheduling over existing events.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The user can start the Google OAuth flow.
- [ ] The callback validates state and handles provider errors.
- [ ] Access and refresh tokens are stored securely.
- [ ] Expired access tokens can be refreshed.
- [ ] The user can disconnect the integration.
- [ ] OAuth status handling is tested without requiring live provider calls.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Configure Google OAuth credentials.
- [ ] Implement connect and callback routes.
- [ ] Encrypt stored tokens.
- [ ] Implement token refresh and disconnect.
- [ ] Add mocked tests.

issues.title: Sync and cache Google Calendar events
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can sync calendar events and continue using cached events when Google is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Connected users can fetch calendar events.
- [ ] Successful results are cached with a last-synced timestamp.
- [ ] Failed requests retry with bounded backoff.
- [ ] Cached data is used when live sync fails.
- [ ] The UI distinguishes live, cached, syncing, and error states.
- [ ] Sync and fallback behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Implement calendar API client.
- [ ] Add cache storage.
- [ ] Add retry and fallback logic.
- [ ] Add sync endpoint and UI state.
- [ ] Add mocked tests.

issues.title: Connect and import assignments from Notion
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can connect Notion and import tasks so that I do not have to enter every assignment manually.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The user can complete Notion OAuth.
- [ ] Tokens are stored securely.
- [ ] The user can choose a database or source.
- [ ] Notion properties can be mapped to PlanGuard assignment fields.
- [ ] Imported assignments belong to the signed-in user.
- [ ] Existing provider IDs prevent duplicate imports.
- [ ] Import and OAuth behavior is tested with mocks.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Implement OAuth connect and callback.
- [ ] Build source selection and property mapping.
- [ ] Implement import service.
- [ ] Add duplicate detection and caching.
- [ ] Add tests.

issues.title: Show truthful integration status
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can see accurate integration status so that I know whether my plan is current.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disconnected integrations show Connect.
- [ ] Active synchronization shows Syncing.
- [ ] Synced appears only after a successful sync.
- [ ] Cached fallback displays Using cached data.
- [ ] Errors include a useful next action.
- [ ] Last successful sync time is displayed.
- [ ] Users can disconnect an integration.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Define integration state model.
- [ ] Replace placeholder Ready labels.
- [ ] Add status and disconnect endpoints.
- [ ] Add UI-state tests.

issues.title: Add JSON API layer
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I can use consistent JSON endpoints so that the frontend and future integrations can interact with PlanGuard reliably.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Assignment CRUD endpoints are available.
- [ ] Focus-session endpoints are available.
- [ ] A priority explanation endpoint is available.
- [ ] Integration connect, status, and sync endpoints are available where appropriate.
- [ ] Validation errors use a consistent JSON shape.
- [ ] Authorization is enforced on every user-owned resource.
- [ ] Success and failure cases are tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Define API response and error conventions.
- [ ] Implement endpoint blueprints.
- [ ] Add server-side validation.
- [ ] Add API tests.

issues.title: Add Alembic or Flask-Migrate migrations
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I can run database migrations so that schema changes are controlled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Flask-Migrate or Alembic is configured.
- [ ] An initial migration captures the current schema.
- [ ] Production does not rely on startup-only db.create_all().
- [ ] Local and production database settings are supported.
- [ ] Migration commands are documented.
- [ ] Optional seed data is available for demos.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add migration dependency and configuration.
- [ ] Generate and review initial migration.
- [ ] Remove production startup table creation.
- [ ] Add seed command or script.
- [ ] Document usage.

issues.title: Harden security and privacy controls
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, my credentials and integration tokens are protected so that my data remains private.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Secrets come from secure environment configuration.
- [ ] Passwords are hashed.
- [ ] Forms use CSRF protection.
- [ ] Session cookies use appropriate security flags.
- [ ] OAuth credentials are encrypted at rest.
- [ ] Sensitive provider data is not written to logs.
- [ ] Authentication routes have basic rate limiting.
- [ ] Security-critical behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Audit secret and session configuration.
- [ ] Add CSRF protection.
- [ ] Implement token encryption.
- [ ] Sanitize provider error logging.
- [ ] Add auth rate limiting.
- [ ] Add security tests.

issues.title: Expand automated test coverage
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I can run a comprehensive test suite so that core PlanGuard workflows are protected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover authentication.
- [ ] Tests cover assignment CRUD and user isolation.
- [ ] Tests cover form and API validation.
- [ ] Tests cover focus-session lifecycle.
- [ ] Tests cover integration statuses and cached fallback.
- [ ] Tests cover priority explanations.
- [ ] Tests cover dashboard empty, loading, overdue, completed, and error states.
- [ ] The suite can run reliably in local development and CI.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Add fixtures and test factories.
- [ ] Add missing unit, integration, and route tests.
- [ ] Add coverage reporting.
- [ ] Configure CI test execution.

issues.title: Improve accessibility and responsive behavior
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I can use PlanGuard on mobile and with keyboard navigation so that it works in my normal study environment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interactive elements are keyboard accessible.
- [ ] Dialog focus is managed correctly.
- [ ] Visible focus indicators are present.
- [ ] Controls have screen-reader labels.
- [ ] Text and controls meet reasonable contrast requirements.
- [ ] Assignment rows, panels, forms, and buttons work on small screens.
- [ ] Text does not overflow.
- [ ] Accessibility and responsive states are manually or automatically checked.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Audit semantic HTML and keyboard behavior.
- [ ] Add dialog focus management.
- [ ] Improve responsive layouts.
- [ ] Add accessibility checks.

issues.title: Handle dashboard empty, loading, and error states
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I receive useful feedback in every dashboard state so that I always understand what to do next.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First-time users receive a clear onboarding action.
- [ ] No-assignment state offers an Add assignment action.
- [ ] Loading is visibly represented.
- [ ] Sync failures explain whether cached data is active.
- [ ] Overdue and completed assignments are clearly represented.
- [ ] A Nothing urgent state is available.
- [ ] State behavior is tested.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Define dashboard state rules.
- [ ] Build state-specific components or templates.
- [ ] Add state tests.

issues.title: Clean up UI copy and encoding
issues.body:
## User story

As a student, I see consistent and correctly rendered text so that the interface feels reliable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Templates render punctuation and symbols correctly in supported browsers.
- [ ] Mojibake or broken characters are removed.
- [ ] Landing page, dashboard, and integration-state copy use consistent terminology.
- [ ] Source files use a consistent encoding.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] Audit templates and static content.
- [ ] Normalize files to UTF-8.
- [ ] Centralize or document preferred UI terminology.
